title: Notification inbox
description: Server-side in-app notification inbox (the bell menu): idempotent publish, newest-first cursor paging, unread counts, mark read, mark all read, archive and retention pruning, scoped to each user's own tenant, with injected persistence and a Fetch Request/Response adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and Web Crypto (crypto.randomUUID) plus the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route. The bell UI and real-time push are left to the receiving app.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: Implement InboxStore on your database: an index on (tenant_id, user_id, created_at DESC, id DESC), a unique partial index on (tenant_id, user_id, dedupe_key), and updateMany as one UPDATE scoped by tenant_id and user_id (the SQL shape is in core.ts).
Call publish(recipient, notification) only from trusted server code after deciding who should be told; it is not exposed over HTTP.
Implement authenticate(request) from your session or verified token, returning the user's id and active tenant id; never read them from the request.
Optionally pass authorize(actor, action) to refuse removed members or suspended tenants.
Set retentionMs and maxPerUser, and run prune() from a scheduled job.
Mount createInboxHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins; it complements, not replaces, your CSRF policy.
limitations: Does not render the bell or list UI, push real-time updates (WebSocket, SSE) or send email, SMS or mobile push.
Does not decide who receives a notification or honor user preferences; check those (see the notification-preferences module) before calling publish.
Titles and bodies are plain text; render them as text, never as HTML.
Cursors are opaque but unsigned; they only position within the actor's own items.
The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only.
No rate limiting; add request rate limits (see the rate-limit module) and cap publish volume in your own code.
Production database correctness, session security and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.

behaviors: list returns newest first and the opaque cursor pages without gaps or repeats, including timestamp ties
a repeated dedupeKey for the same recipient returns the existing item, also under concurrent publishes
a dedupeKey is independent per user and reusable after the retention window
unread counts follow markRead, markAllRead (with an optional before time) and archive
markRead keeps the first read time and ignores unknown ids
another user's or another tenant's ids are never read, marked or archived
javascript:, data:, http:, protocol-relative and credential-bearing links are rejected
title, kind, body, dedupeKey and data size are validated; stored data is a detached copy
prune drops items past retention and the oldest beyond maxPerUser per user
HTTP adapter: routes and status codes, 401 when signed out, origin check on writes, no publish route, no-store responses

changes: First release: core, in-memory store and Fetch adapter.
